Performance report: RGood on de_nuke

1-bb5c8d4a-54a5-47c5-a540-5b05181dcdf9-1-1.dem. 23 rounds, 10-13. One metric: impact. Good plays count positive, mistakes count negative, and every number shows its arithmetic.

RGood finished 10-13 on de_nuke with an average impact of -11.3 per round, a negative game: 14 plays worth +574 against 14 mistakes worth -834. The positive side was driven by utility on a signal (5, +200) and trade kill (2, +78). The biggest costs were isolated before dying (4, -273) and died anchoring (2, -101). By side, -17 per round on CT and -6 per round on T, so the T half carried the game. The best round was R9 (+156) and the worst was R14 (-179); 8 rounds produced nothing either way. Removing the isolated before dying flags alone would have moved the average to +0.6 per round.

Isolated before dying (4, impact -273)

Why it is a mistake: In the 10 s before this death you and your nearest teammate moved apart, with two or more teammates still alive. This is the avoidable kind of untraded death: the gap was created by movement, not by the round state.
What to do instead: When you move, move toward or with a teammate. If you have to go alone, go for a delay or information, not a duel.

Died anchoring (2, impact -101)

Why it is a mistake: Sometimes unavoidable: the anchor dies when three players hit the site. It still costs the round when it happens early, without damage, or without a call.
What to do instead: Delay rather than duel: utility first, fall back to a crossfire spot, call the rotate at the first sound, and make them spend time on you.

Early solo T contact (1, impact -72)

Why it is a mistake: Contact before 20 s with nobody near you means the CT is set up and you are not. You had dealt no damage, so the round started a man down with no information.
What to do instead: No contact in the first 20 s unless the team's utility has landed and a teammate is on your shoulder.

Utility thrown too early (1, impact -70)

Why it is a mistake: A smoke or molotov thrown with no enemy within 30 m, none spotted by your team, and usually before the T side could even reach that choke. Later in the same round you were in contact for 4 s or more with no delay grenade left. The throw was on the clock, not on information.
What to do instead: Hold the delay grenade until one of these exists: enemies seen or heard at the choke, a teammate's call, or the enemy's timing from earlier rounds. Before the earliest possible T arrival at that choke, nothing you throw is reacting to anything.

Died with usable utility (1, impact -69)

Why it is a mistake: Only counted when three things were true after contact: there was time (2 s for a flash or HE with the killer inside 30 m, 4 s for a smoke or molotov), there was a safe throw window of at least 1.5 s in which no nearby enemy was visible to your team, you were not visible to theirs, and you were not being hit, and the grenade would have done something. If the enemy could engage you the whole time, throwing would have been the mistake, and the grenade is not counted.
What to do instead: Once contact is called and you are delaying, the usable grenades go out in the first seconds, not after the fight is lost. Flash the choke, HE the stack, molotov the entrance, then fight.

Utility on a timer (1, impact -54)

Why it is a mistake: The same grenade from the same spot at the same second every round tells the enemy where you stand and when the choke is covered. They time their push to it.
What to do instead: Throw on sound and on information, not on the clock. Some rounds throw nothing before 20 s and hold the angle instead.

Long-distance spray missed (1, impact -51)

Why it is a mistake: Only counted when the shots in the 4 s before the death include a continuous run of 7 or more at the weapon's cycle rate, at 20 m or more, with 20 damage or less to the killer. Bursts and taps are a different flag.
What to do instead: Past 20 m fire 2 to 3 bullets, stop, counter-strafe, fire again. Never more than 4 without a reset.

Died flashed (1, impact -50)

Why it is a mistake: A blinded player is a free kill. Either you pushed through a flash you saw coming, or a teammate blinded you.
What to do instead: When a flash is thrown at your position, turn away and hold the corner. Call 'flashing' before your own throws and do not walk into teammates' flashes.

Traded by enemy (1, impact -48)

Why it is a mistake: After a kill everyone knows where you are, and the next enemy is already aiming at that spot. Re-peeking or staying is the deadliest 50-50 in the game.
What to do instead: After every kill, move at least one position before the next fight. Take the trade only if a teammate is already swinging with you.
